blocks.content: To save you hunting for a good example, we've filled in a ready-made query that lands you on a set of traces worth reading. That query is written in TraceQL, Tempo's trace query language. You'll learn what it is in a couple of slides. For now, you don't need to read or write it. Just run it and open one of the results.
Run the ready-made query. It opens Explore and returns a list of candidate traces, all of them the same kind of request, so any one is a good one to read.
Now, open any trace in the results list by clicking its trace ID. Every result is the same shape, so it doesn't matter which one you pick.

You're now looking at the **trace view**: one request laid out as a **span waterfall**, with each row a span stacked by when it started. Read it top-down. The top row is the request itself, and everything nested below is the work it set off.

Don't worry that the durations or trace look different from any screenshot. The demo streams live data, so every trace is a little different. What stays the same is the shape, and that's what you're here to read.
